artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan building a PTY-proxying wrapper in lua/neotex/plugins/ai/sapience/ that inserts separators into sf1's output stream, with a validated styling option and graceful fallback to the bare sf1 command.

memory_candidates.content: When a Neovim config owns only a terminal window's placement and the content comes from an untracked, self-updating vendor CLI, a PTY-proxying wrapper (pty.openpty + setsid + TIOCSCTTY + raw-mode stdin forwarding) is the only interposition point that is both durable (versioned in the consuming repo) and non-destructive (never writes to the vendor payload). A shell pipe is NOT a substitute: it turns the child's stdout into a non-tty, disabling color detection and readline line editing. Two non-obvious hazards govern the filter design: (1) GNU readline re-emits the prompt on every line edit, so prompt-pattern matching must count a prompt as fresh only when reached via \n, never via \r, with a one-shot latch; (2) a transient \r\033[2K status indicator must suppress injection until cleared. The robust design for the question/answer boundary avoids output pattern matching entirely by keying on the input side (the forwarded CR/LF keystroke). Failure mode must be pass-through-on-no-match, so a vendor output change yields 'no dividers' rather than a broken pane.
